summary:
W2-OPS is finished. All 13 brief IDs are fixed. I also found and fixed one new defect: a QA scratch server kept its connections to the live ui-api open after SIGTERM. On timing: nothing more is needed from me. What remains for the PM is applying 6 small patch requests (one test line, five lines of README text), about 10 to 15 minutes including the gate re-runs.

- **Live incident (not caused by a fix, already reported to main):** from about 14:40 IST the live ui-api (pid 75525) stopped accepting connections. Connects timed out, it sat at 0% CPU, and :8010 had 208 open connections, mostly from the agents' scratch relays. 6 of them were mine: my stopped scratch server had ignored SIGTERM, so I SIGKILLed it. I restarted nothing. ui-api is now healthy as pid 70501 (I did not do that restart). Because of this, scratch_server.py now has a bounded shutdown and closes its upstream connections, with a regression test.
- **start-local.sh** (installed with temp file + mv; bash -n passes on /bin/bash 3.2.57; live `status` and `help` exit 0 and stay read-only):
  - The `ui-release` row shows the release in ui/dist/current next to the one ui-api serves (GET /version). It warns `mismatch` when they differ.
  - The `prefs` row reads ui-api's durable migration record from the store's meta table, using W2-API's real schema, with the API as fallback. After the import it stays `imported` even when every key is later edited in the app; the record's 'inferred' backfill is supported.
  - The per-record fallback gains an `app-owned` state with no misleading instruction, and the instruction now names only the keys an import can still fill.
  - The status Python has a 10 s timeout: GNU timeout, or a bash fallback when it is missing.
  - `rotate_log` now fails closed: it leaves a log alone when lsof is missing, fails, or prints unexpected output.
  - START_SET nit fixed.
- **QA tools:**
  - scratch_server.py sends X-Forwarded-Host as Next does, so same-origin QA POSTs now pass the real guard while cross-site ones are still refused. Its shutdown is bounded and it closes its upstream client.
  - parity.py and netpolicy.py know the header's NSE holiday lookup, matched by exact query values. They accept both W2-UI-SHELL's shared `?back=0&ahead=7` and round-1's `?back=0&ahead=10`, set it aside only when it appears on one side, and have a `--no-expected-deltas` switch. A browser smoke run confirmed it: set aside on watch/desk/stocks, still compared on brief/eco.
  - e2e_multiwin.py has the two-window Compare case and `--scenarios`; a crashing scenario now counts as a FAIL.
  - delta_probe.py aborts every non-GET /api request.
- **Baseline tools:**
  - reconstruct.py pins every recorded input. The D3.md BOM may be in either form; the old and the corrected D3.md give the same digest.
  - It now refuses an unrecorded edit anywhere in a touched file made after that file's last recorded change, and checks the PM backup's mtimes.
  - Its docstring states the one window it cannot see: an edit made before a file's last recorded change.
  - The BOM test now accepts the corrected D3.md.
  - Re-run on FX-QA's real snapshot with --pm-backup: every check passes, and MANIFEST and the diff patch are byte-identical.
- **CI and contract tests (completeness-05):**
  - The desktop contract tests now FAIL on a missing or reshaped source, unless DESKTOP_CONTRACT_ALLOW_SKIP=1 is set.
  - ci.yml has a new macOS `desktop` job: cargo fmt/clippy/test, the boot-page checks, the ui/scripts tests, the shell tests, the strict contract tests and a real static export. The ui job runs on node 25 and finds every plain-node check file itself (it picked up W2-UI-PAGES' new pages.check.ts), and the baseline tools run too.
  - A new tests/integration/test_desktop_ci.py guards against CI drift.
- **RUNBOOK:**
  - §7 now matches the guard: tailnet devices are remote, so read-only by default; GUARD_ALLOW_REMOTE_WRITES=1 is optional, with its consequences; GUARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is not needed.
  - §8 explains the prefs row's states.
  - §4 explains the ui-release row.
- **E2E after AUDIT2_DONE** (scratch servers with --prefs-db, GET-only to live): a copy of the live round-1 release fails Compare in both engines while watchlist and gold pass, which reproduces the bug. A scratch build of the current source (W2-UI-PAGES' Compare fix) passes all 6 runs (3 scenarios × 2 engines).

Gates: core 586 passed / 9 skipped. scripts/tests: 175 passed, 1 failed, the job-set assertion in test_ci_workflow.py; PR-W2-OPS-1 fixes it (the patched test was checked: 2 passed). Baseline tools 24. ui-api 793. ruff and mypy are clean on everything I touched. Negative controls on the pre-change files: ops tests 20 of 24 fail, baseline-tool tests 20 of 24 fail, the old contract file skips 21 tests silently in a partial tree, and the SIGTERM test hangs with the old scratch server.

findings.what_changed: start-local.sh prefs_summary_py/prefs_status_row: reads the durable K2 migration record. First from the store's meta table (W2-API's real schema: table meta(k, v), JSON row 'migration'; a key/value shape is also accepted), then from GET /api/prefs `migration` when the table is absent. ui-api is asked only for the store it actually uses, i.e. never when PREFS_DB is set in the caller's environment. Rules: imported = the record has legacy_import_at, shown as 'imported N keys from <origin> on <date> IST', or 'imported from <origin> (recorded from its N records; earliest …)' when the record says inferred. It never flips back after app edits. Without a record (older ui-api) a non-provisional :3000 row still counts as imported, unchanged. A provisional :3000 row never counts. The keys an import can still fill (absent, or default-only) are named in the → line. Both keys set in the app: 'not imported' with an 'other settings' instruction when the record says no import, or the neutral 'app-owned' with no instruction when there is no record. Values are never printed; the store is opened read-only (mode=ro or immutable), so no -wal/-shm is left.
findings.tests: tests/integration/test_desktop_ops.py, 11 cases: K2 meta JSON in ui-api's (k, v) and a (key, value) table, plus individual keys, after every key was edited in the app; K2 'no import' with open and with closed keys; app-owned with no record; a provisional :3000 row is not an import; K2 from the API fallback; an explicit PREFS_DB never asks ui-api (the fake server sees no /api/prefs). Against W2-API's REAL prefs.py store: migrated then edited stays imported; never migrated; backfilled-inferred. scripts/tests/test_ops_shell.py still 19 passed. Negative control on the pre-change script: all K2 cases fail.
findings.user_visible_change: The `./start-local.sh status` prefs row can now read 'imported … · imported N keys from http://localhost:3000 on <date> IST', a new neutral 'app-owned' state, and a → line naming only the watchlist and/or pins that are still open (or an 'other settings' line).

findings.what_changed: log_writers now returns 'ok <writers> <non-append>' or 'error <why>'. A missing lsof, an exit other than 0, exit 1 with any output, any 'lsof:' message, or a line that is not a -F p/f/G field all count as error. Only exit 1 with no output at all means 'no writers'. On error rotate_log leaves the file alone and reports 'not rotating <log> (<size> bytes): cannot tell whether a process still writes it (<why>); left as is'.
findings.tests: test_rotation_is_skipped_when_lsof_is_missing (a PATH holding only the needed tools, minus lsof), test_rotation_is_skipped_when_lsof_fails (fake lsof: a stderr warning with exit 1, exit 2, garbage output with exit 0), and the control test_rotation_still_renames_a_log_nobody_has_open (exit 1, silent). The existing test_rotate_logs_renames_copytruncates_or_skips still passes. The 4 fail-closed cases fail against the pre-change script.
findings.user_visible_change: rotate-logs (watchdog hourly, or each start) may print a 'cannot tell whether a process still writes it' line instead of renaming a log, when lsof is missing or fails.

findings.what_changed: main(): the prerequisite and dependency checks of `start` and of a full `restart` now use ${START_SET:-$CORE_SERVICES}, the same set start_services iterates. So a START_SET that includes frontend gets its npm check and npm install.
findings.tests: test_prerequisite_checks_see_the_start_set, 4 cases: start/restart, each with and without START_SET. stop_services and check_prerequisites are overridden, so nothing starts or stops. The 2 START_SET cases fail against the pre-change script.

findings.what_changed: New run_with_timeout helper. It uses GNU timeout -k 2 when present (it signals the whole process group); otherwise a bash 3.2 wait loop that TERMs, then KILLs 2 s later, the command and its direct children. The status Python gets STATUS_PY_TIMEOUT seconds (default 10). The program is passed with -c (no stdin or heredoc into a background job). A timeout shows 'unreadable … <python> timed out after 10s (blocked on a macOS privacy prompt?)'.
findings.tests: test_a_hanging_status_python_times_out[True/False]: a fake python that execs `sleep 30`, STATUS_PY_TIMEOUT=1, with GNU timeout and with the bash fallback. Both return in under 10 s (measured 1.0 s and 3.3 s). Both fail against the pre-change script.
findings.user_visible_change: A hung status Python now shows the prefs row as 'unreadable … timed out' after 10 s instead of hanging `status`.

findings.what_changed: scratch_server.py has a new forward_headers() used by forward(). Like Next's /api rewrite, it drops hop-by-hop headers and Host (httpx sets the backend's) and sends the page's Host as X-Forwarded-Host, replacing any value the client sent. Origin is unchanged. A same-origin QA write therefore passes shared/http_guard.py; a cross-site one is still refused at the backend. --block-mutations is unchanged.
findings.tests: test_desktop_qa_harness.py, in front of a FastAPI backend wrapped in the REAL install_http_guard: test_forward_headers_are_what_nexts_rewrite_sends; test_scratch_proxy_same_origin_write_reaches_the_guarded_backend (200; the backend sees host 127.0.0.1:8010 and x-forwarded-host 127.0.0.1:8093; a spoofed client X-Forwarded-Host is replaced); test_scratch_proxy_does_not_launder_a_cross_site_write (403 'unauthorized', both a foreign Origin and Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site); and the negative control test_without_x_forwarded_host_the_guard_refuses_the_same_write (pre-fix behaviour gives 403). Live browser use: E2E and parity smoke through the relay, GETs only to :8010.
findings.user_visible_change: None (QA tool). Non-blocked POSTs through a scratch server no longer get a guard 403.

findings.what_changed: RUNBOOK §7 rewritten against the current shared/http_guard.py, including W2-API's X-Forwarded-For rule. Points: Serve keeps the ts.net Host, so only GUARD_ALLOWED_HOSTS is needed; GUARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS is redundant because Origin equals the allowed Host. Every tailnet device is REMOTE, since Serve sets X-Forwarded-For whatever uvicorn's proxy-header setting is. Remote devices are read-only by default: pages, quotes and the monitor WebSocket work; prefs writes, compute POSTs, paper orders and Desk actions get 403 'clients on other machines are read-only', and phone edits stay on the phone. GUARD_ALLOW_REMOTE_WRITES=1 is an explicit opt-in, with the consequence spelled out: everything the terminal can do, so only if every tailnet device is yours. Restart ui-api after changes, respecting the freeze windows. §8 documents the prefs row states (imported, not imported, app-owned, unreadable/timeout). §4 documents the ui-release row and its mismatch.
findings.tests: Documentation, checked line by line against shared/http_guard.py (evaluate(), _client_is_local, _forwarded_for_is_local, _same_origin) and prefs.py's K2 docstring. Tailscale is not installed here, so the Serve commands themselves are untested.
findings.user_visible_change: RUNBOOK text: tailnet access is documented as read-only by default, with an opt-in to writes.

findings.what_changed: netpolicy.py: new EXPECTED_DELTAS / expected_delta(). The header's NSE holiday lookup is GET /api/market/eco-calendar with the exact query back=0&ahead=7 (W2-UI-SHELL's shared ECO_SHARED_QUERY, which is also BRIEF's own query) or back=0&ahead=10 (round-1 releases). It is matched on query values, so the ECO and EVTS pages' own calls are still compared. probe.summarize marks an endpoint expected_delta only when EVERY call of it was such a request. parity.compare sets a one-sided expected endpoint aside into diff.expected_deltas plus a note; the summary and markdown list the tabs. New --no-expected-deltas switch; meta records it. A drift-guard test reads holidays.ts and api.ts, so a changed query fails a test instead of turning parity DIFF. Lint: parity.py's pre-existing I001/RUF100 and probe.py's 12 BLE001/S110 are now fixed or carry a reasoned noqa.
findings.tests: test_expected_delta_matches_method_path_and_exact_query_values; test_netpolicy_knows_the_query_the_ui_actually_sends (drift guard); test_compare_sets_a_one_sided_expected_delta_aside_and_reports_it (also the strict mode, and an endpoint with other calls is still compared); test_summarize_marks_an_endpoint_expected_only_when_every_call_is; test_parity_cli_has_the_expected_delta_switch. (1) RECORDS_SHA256 pins every recorded input: the parsed D4/D3 blocks (BOM normalised), d3_callsites pairs, Write hashes and originals; check_records() also checks the originals against provenance.json. A changed patch block is refused; a change to prose is accepted. So an unrecorded edit anywhere in a touched file made after that record is refused; this is the adversarial reviewer's exact case. patch_requests.new: assert set(doc["jobs"]) == {"python", "ui", "desktop"}   # desktop: the macOS gates of the desktop program (completeness-05)
patch_requests.why: completeness-05 adds a macOS 'desktop' job to ci.yml (cargo, boot checks, ui/scripts tests, shell tests, the static export). Without this one-line change scripts/tests has 1 failure. Every other needle in the test is still present. A temp copy with this change applied: 2 passed.

patch_requests.old:
Every reversal asserts that the text it removes occurs **exactly once**. An unrecorded change therefore makes the
script fail; it cannot drift.
patch_requests.new:
Every reversal asserts that the text it removes occurs **exactly once**, so an edit inside a recorded block makes
the script fail. Outside the blocks the snapshot's mtimes are checked: every file no record touches must predate the
program, and every touched file must be dated at the time of the last record that changed it (±slack), so an
unrecorded edit made after that record, anywhere in the file, also fails (`tools/test_reconstruct.py`
`test_unrecorded_edit_outside_the_recorded_blocks_of_a_touched_file_is_refused`). The recorded inputs themselves
(the parsed D3.md/D4.md blocks and `records/`) are pinned by sha256 (`RECORDS_SHA256`). What the snapshot cannot show
is an edit outside the blocks made *before* a file's last recorded change; that window is covered by the transcript
scans (`records/program_writes.tsv`, `records/bash_write_scan.tsv`) and by the PM backup, whose files must equal the
intermediate state and be dated before the program or at a recorded change.
patch_requests.why: FX-QA adversarial check: the README overclaimed drift detection. reconstruct.py now proves what is stated here (W2-OPS) and its docstring names the remaining window; the README must say the same.

patch_requests.old:
`records/` holds every piece of evidence the reversal reads, with provenance (transcript, tool_use id and UTC
timestamp in `records/provenance.json`).
patch_requests.new:
`records/` holds every piece of evidence the reversal reads, with provenance (transcript, tool_use id and UTC
timestamp in `records/provenance.json`), except the D4.md and D3.md blocks, which `tools/reconstruct.py` reads from
